gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Autel EVO II Dual 640T V3 bundles are listed $400 lower at autelpilot.com today ($4,399 Rugged, $4,899 Enterprise) than on Autel's own shop ($4,799 / $5,299), which puts the Rugged Bundle $1,000 under the $5,399 RTK V3 ChatGPT recommended.
standout_why: Compared against blog.dronetrader.com/thermal-drones-for-sale (dated Oct 10 prices for 8 models), nighthunting.net/thermal-drones (36 models with prices), bestthermaldrone.com best / cost / compare (price bands only, plus a drawback per model) and maverickdrone.com/pages/thermal-drones. Between them the category is already priced and each model already has a stated drawback. What they lack: dronetrader and nighthunting quote only Autel's own-shop prices for the EVO II Dual 640T V3 ($4,799 / $5,299, and $5,799 for the RTK), not the $400-lower autelpilot.com listings, and none works out the dollar steps between models. One limit on my side: the autelpilot, Autel shop, Night Vision Outfitters and Maverick prices were read from each store's own search listing today; the individual product pages returned HTTP 429, so variants, box contents and stock are not verified on the product pages.
decides: It confirms the Autel picks and changes which one to recommend. EVO Lite 640T Basic Combo is $3,359 at every seller checked, so it stays the cheapest new 640 × 512 drone. For the middle pick, the EVO II Dual 640T V3 Rugged Bundle at $4,399 is $1,000 less than the RTK V3 ChatGPT showed at $5,399, and only loses if the shopper needs RTK or a speaker (that configuration does not accept them). The Enterprise Bundle at $4,899 is harder to defend: the EVO Max 4T V2 is $800 more at $5,699 and adds 10× optical zoom, a laser rangefinder and 42 minutes. DJI Matrice 4T stays the top-spec pick at $6,965 and up, with the warranty and FCC caveats below.
